# HorizontalLinePath { #timetoalign.loader.graphical.HorizontalLinePath }

```python
loader.graphical.HorizontalLinePath(x0, x1, y, tolerance=10.0)
```

Time axis as a horizontal line at fixed y.

The simplest case: x directly maps to time coordinate.
This is the typical case for musical scores, spectrograms,
and most graphical analyses.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name      | Type                                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                      |
|-----------|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| x0        | [Number](`timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths.Number`) | Starting x coordinate (left edge).                                                                                                                               |
| x1        | [Number](`timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths.Number`) | Ending x coordinate (right edge).                                                                                                                                |
| y         | [Number](`timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths.Number`) | Fixed y coordinate (vertical position of the line).                                                                                                              |
| tolerance | [Number](`timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths.Number`) | The half-breadth of the strip the line stands for: the strip spans ``y - tolerance`` to ``y + tolerance``, and :meth:`from_2d` answers for the points within it. |

Every number is kept as given: integers (and ``Fraction`` values) give
exact answers.

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

Pixel coordinates stay integral, so the geometry answers in whole
pixels rather than widening to float:

```python
>>> path = HorizontalLinePath(x0=10, x1=500, y=100)
>>> path.length
490
>>> path.to_2d(0)
(10, 100)
>>> path.to_2d(245)
(255, 100)
>>> path.from_2d(255, 100)
245
```

## Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [distance_to_path](#timetoalign.loader.graphical.HorizontalLinePath.distance_to_path) | Distance is simply \|y - self.y\| if x is in range. |
| [from_2d](#timetoalign.loader.graphical.HorizontalLinePath.from_2d) | Map (x, y) to timeline coordinate. |
| [to_2d](#timetoalign.loader.graphical.HorizontalLinePath.to_2d) | Map timeline coordinate to (x, y). |

### distance_to_path { #timetoalign.loader.graphical.HorizontalLinePath.distance_to_path }

```python
loader.graphical.HorizontalLinePath.distance_to_path(x, y)
```

Distance is simply |y - self.y| if x is in range.

### from_2d { #timetoalign.loader.graphical.HorizontalLinePath.from_2d }

```python
loader.graphical.HorizontalLinePath.from_2d(x, y)
```

Map (x, y) to timeline coordinate.

Returns None if:
- y is outside the strip ``y ± tolerance``
- x is outside the [x0, x1] range

### to_2d { #timetoalign.loader.graphical.HorizontalLinePath.to_2d }

```python
loader.graphical.HorizontalLinePath.to_2d(coord)
```

Map timeline coordinate to (x, y).
